cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: arcsine of -0.5 in radians (-pi/6)
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as -0.523598776. Independently verified in Python: math.asin(-0.5) = -0.5235987755982989, which is exactly -pi/6 -> -0.523598776 at 9 dp

cases.description: The same example converted to degrees, as the documented Remark suggests
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as -30. Independently verified: -pi/6 radians = -30 degrees exactly; the double-precision product is -30.000000000000004, which is -30 at 9 dp

cases.description: An argument above 1 is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that number "must be from -1 to 1"; an argument outside the domain of a real-valued math function is Excel's documented #NUM! case
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the ACOT page states it explicitly for this inverse-trigonometric family
